conclusion: Current tiny-body purchase scaling remains dominated by shared driver work, not one planner loop: publication is about31-33% of sampled userCPU at8/16workers, planning about21-24%, reservations about10-12%, and driver sample share about75-77%. Total ordinary-binary task-clock/request rises materially with worker count.

provenance.normal_vs_fp: Normal frozen binary supplies PMU/software counters and diagnostics. FP build supplies attribution only; no new ordinary throughput benchmark was run.

planning_parallelism_boundary.potential_read_only_work: Candidate row enumeration, read-only join lookup/product construction, memo comparisons, dependency/key/access descriptions against captured immutable snapshot+memo are potential distributed candidate-generation work. Measured planning share is not a guaranteed parallelizable fraction.
planning_parallelism_boundary.ordering_and_state_constraints: Provider-before-bound join order, per-pass scratch ownership, fallback component slot registration and candidate ordering need preservation. Admission/reservation mutation and run-ID allocation remain coordinated after candidate generation.
planning_parallelism_boundary.publication_boundary: Live-world freshness validation, write-revision reconciliation, command application, derived owner/index cleanup and memo publication observe/mutate current world and must remain consistent with commit ordering. They cannot simply be moved to a stale snapshot worker check.
planning_parallelism_boundary.concrete_followup_hypothesis: spawn_slots call-context sample share rises from~0.3% at1worker to~2.4-2.9% at8/16, while finish_derived_spawns adds~1-1.6%. Source shows shared spawn-bookkeeping Mutex touched even for no-spawn invocations. A narrow skip/lazy-acquisition experiment is better supported than assuming all planner work is the scaling bottleneck; samples do not prove contention.

limitations: Sixteen independent100-round FP recordings: async/sync x1/4/8/16workers x2processes,5warmup rounds,1000slots,statsOFF. No extra recordings after consistency.
FP changes optimization/layout and timing; its phase fractions cannot be multiplied by normal PMU/task-clock to claim exact physical driverCPU time.

Normal core counters have2processes/configuration,100%coverage. Software task-clock has1process/configuration,100%coverage,aggregate across all threads; no per-thread task-clock available in existing runner.
Cycle, instruction and task-clock increases can suggest coordination/cache/stall costs but cannot identify a specific lock or cacheline without a focused controlled experiment.
Exclusive ownership uses nearest recognized actual outer function, ignoring generic nested names. Other/unknown remains explicit; mechanisms and context tags are separate overlapping dimensions.
Admission includes reservation release. Worker row execution/completion/kernel boundaries depend on inlining; resolved kernelbody share is not total business-logic cost.
Publication includes command application of measured input/derived paths; phase subcosts with ambiguous callers remain other.
revision_for_entity generic symbols may be identical-code-folded to Stamp; no claim that Stamp data is active.
On-CPU sampling does not measure time blocked off-CPU. Command-producer operation tags are not all lock cost; explicit lock primitive symbols were not resolved there.
Explicit Arc clone/drop tags miss inlined atomic operations and cannot establish negligible total reference-count cost.
No source edits, new builds, commits or engine optimization by benchmark agent.
